questions.question: A component reads only `user` from a Context whose value is `{ user, cartCount }`. What happens when `cartCount` changes?
options: Nothing, Context compares the fields the component used
The component re-renders, because every consumer re-renders when the provider value changes
Only components that read cartCount re-render
React throws a warning about unused context fields
questions.explanation: Context has no selector mechanism. When the value object changes, every component using that context re-renders.

questions.question: Which kind of state is TanStack Query designed to manage?
options: Server state: a cache of remote data with refetching and invalidation
questions.explanation: TanStack Query is a server-state cache keyed by queryKey. It is not a general client-state store.

questions.question: Which is a genuine advantage of Redux over Zustand for large, multi-team apps?
options: Every change is a named, serialisable action, enabling time-travel debugging, action logs and many features reacting to one event
Redux needs fewer lines of code for a simple store
questions.explanation: Redux's explicit action events and middleware give predictability and tooling. Zustand is usually less code and needs no provider.

questions.question: Your app already uses Redux Toolkit and you want one devtools view of all state including API data. Which data-fetching choice fits best?
options: TanStack Query with a separate QueryClient
Storing fetch results in React Context
RTK Query, which keeps its cache in the Redux store and shows actions in Redux DevTools
Plain useEffect plus useState in every component
questions.explanation: RTK Query lives in the Redux store under its reducerPath, so its requests and cache appear in Redux DevTools alongside the rest of the state.
